rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract rather than from evidence. Geometry: five line sensors spread across x = -0.04 to +0.04 m (8 mm spacing of 2 cm) and placed 4 cm ahead of the axle, so they see the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 12 mm is a middle value that covers the 25 mm tape with a few sensors at once. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m and mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that keep yaw inertia moderate. Controller: sensor weights are proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so a positive signal (line on the left) steers left, as the contract requires. kp = 1.5 gives a moderate steering response (turn of about 1.5 per unit signal, 525 PWM per unit), kd = 0.1 damps the response, and ki = 0.02 is small to avoid integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.6 (PWM about 80 percent) targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last left the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. Hypotheses to test: (1) speed is too high or kp too low if max_error grows on tight bends; (2) kd too low if steering_oscillation is high; (3) line-loss events indicate sensors too narrow or too few. Next measurements: completion_time and progress tell whether speed is sufficient, max_error and line_loss_events show steering margin, and steering_oscillation shows whether kd is adequate.
